about: Quint's research memory: every strategy tried, its status, its evidence and the verdict, plus the lessons learned and the queue of next experiments. Every lab session reads this first and updates it last. Statuses follow research/mnq/STRATEGY-RESEARCH-PROGRAMME.md. Nothing here is financial advice.

realMoney.note: No bot trades a real or prop account yet. Live trading comes through Quint Control (NinjaTrader 8 on the owner's Windows computer), phases 1 to 3, and every bot needs the owner's confirm before it goes live.

strategies.name: Your strategy: WYLD Will Four Pillars
strategies.timeframe: 1m entries, 15m liquidity, monthly to daily levels
strategies.rules: WYLD Will's four pillars, in order. 1 Liquidity sweep of a 15m pool marked before the open. 2 Price trades into a higher-timeframe level and shows it holds. 3 PDR bias: from Point A (the level that held) to Point B (the next HTF level). 4 A 1-minute confirmation is the entry. Tight stop beyond the wick, break-even fast, Target 1 Point B, Target 2 the opposing liquidity. While the PDR is active each new confirmation is a fresh entry. First 2 to 3 hours after the New York open only. Full checklist: lab/brain/playbooks.json.
strategies.source: The owner's own strategy, from WYLD Will's videos: the WYLD Will System rulebook and the Four Pillars Trainer (claude.ai). The master version. Never remove it.

versions.name: Master: WYLD Will Four Pillars
versions.where: WYLD Will System rulebook and Four Pillars Trainer (claude.ai)

versions.name: TradingView indicator: Quint · WYLD Four Pillars
versions.where: Your TradingView (My scripts); code in lab/pine/wyld_four_pillars.pine
versions.note: Version 2.0: live step-by-step alerts with each step marked on the chart (the wick box of the last push with its 50% and close-beyond trigger, the level that held, the PDR box, entry and stop, how each setup ended), a small confluence box (Detailed in settings) and a regime table for every timeframe. Pools run overnight no longer count as a 9:30 sweep. Signals only; a mechanical reading of the rules with the open choices as settings.

versions.name: Older coding: six steps
versions.note: Differs from WYLD: requires displacement, takes one pullback entry, adds a regime filter. Tested in its Backtest lab and the Jarvis dream run.

versions.name: Older coding: 5 pillars
versions.note: Differs from WYLD: requires displacement and 1.5R of room. 0 trades in 4 weeks.

strategies.verdict: Your main strategy, and WYLD Will's rules are the master. Not backtested as WYLD states it yet: a few rules aren't exact (the easiest equal highs and lows, the stop buffer, the break-even trigger, entries per PDR). The two coded versions in your apps are older and stricter than WYLD (Chart Wizard's took 0 trades in 4 weeks), so they should be brought in line with WYLD's rules. His results are his own claims.

evidence.note: Chart Wizard version. 478 candles at pillar 1, 382 swept, 250 CISD, 106 displaced, 6 confirmed pullbacks, 0 with 1.5R of room.

evidence.where: lab/FACTORY_REPORT.md (strategy factory, family wyld, mechanical v0)
evidence.data: MNQ 5m, 21 Oct to 17 Nov 2026: tuned on 12 sessions, judged on 8 unseen
evidence.note: 1,152 variations (pools x confirmation x stop buffer x target x break-even x window x entries). 156 made money on the unseen sessions, but the best tuned variation lost $1,013 over 7 unseen trades. PBO 37%. Far too little 5-minute data, and no 1-minute data for WYLD's real confirmations yet.

strategies.next: Queue item wyld-exact-rules, then code WYLD's rules once and line the app versions up with them.

strategies.name: 20-candle breakout
strategies.rules: A 15-minute close beyond the last 20 candles; stop 2 ATR; target 3x the stop; out after 40 candles.
strategies.source: Chart Wizard (taught in the app)
strategies.verdict: Beat its costs on 11 weeks of MNQ, but lost money in the first half and made it all in the October to November sell-off, mostly on shorts. One day was 45% of the profit. Promising, not proven.

evidence.note: First half -$420, second half +$6,821. Longest losing streak 10. Matches TradingView's Strategy Tester closely.

strategies.next: Needs a rising market and years of data: NinjaTrader Strategy Analyzer run of bot 3 from 2019.

strategies.name: New York open breakout
strategies.rules: The 9:30 to 9:45 New York range; a close outside it until 11:30; stop on the other side; target 2R; one trade a day.
strategies.source: Chart Wizard (taught in the app)
strategies.verdict: Just over break-even, and only because of one big day. Without that day it lost money. The weakest case for staying in the app.

evidence.note: Best day +$1,581 was more than the total. Longs lost $1,531.

strategies.next: Years of data in NinjaTrader before any decision.

strategies.name: Opening candle direction (5-minute opening range)
strategies.rules: Trade the direction of the 9:30 to 9:35 candle; stop at its other end; target 10R, or out at the close.
strategies.source: Zarattini, Barbon & Aziz, 5-minute opening range breakout paper. A replication on NQ made little after costs (PLAN.md).
strategies.verdict: First read only: 20 trades.

strategies.name: Last-30-minute momentum
strategies.rules: At 15:30 New York, go with the move since yesterday's close; out at the close; 0.5% emergency stop.
strategies.source: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou (JFE 2018); Baltussen, Da, Lammers & Martens (JFE 2021). Plan bot 2: build second.
strategies.verdict: Strong academic evidence over decades, but it lost on the 4 weeks we have. One trade a day, so it needs years to judge.

strategies.name: VWAP trend
strategies.rules: Long above VWAP, short below, flip on every cross; up to 40 trades a day; 0.5% emergency stop.
strategies.source: Zarattini & Aziz. An independent rebuild couldn't get near the paper (PLAN.md).
strategies.verdict: Needs 1-minute candles, which the lab doesn't have. Trades often, so check Lucid's microscalping rule.

strategies.name: Gap fade
strategies.rules: A 0.2% to 1% gap that the first 5-minute candle turns back; target yesterday's close; out by 11:30.
strategies.source: Plan bot 9. Walk-forward on 2 years of MNQ hourly: +$2,145, PF 1.14, but a $3,116 drawdown (DEV Community).
strategies.verdict: Lowest priority. Its published drawdown is bigger than a 50K's max loss.

strategies.name: Inverted fair value gap
strategies.rules: Trend from the 5-minute EMA 50 and 200; the first fair value gap against the trend that price closes through, until 11:30; target 2R; once a day.
strategies.source: Daxton Trades' video; the EMA lengths and the stop are ours.
strategies.verdict: First read only: 12 trades.

strategies.name: Range squeeze breakout
strategies.rules: A 20-minute range tighter than 0.15% and than 90% of yesterday's ranges; a close outside it; target 2R; up to 3 a day.
strategies.source: A NinjaTrader range-breakout bot video; the numbers are ours.
strategies.verdict: Needs 1-minute candles.

strategies.name: Trend-join scalper
strategies.rules: EMA 9 above 21 above 50 with the 21 rising; a dip to the 21 that closes up; target 7 points, stop 24; up to 10 a day.
strategies.source: Shaped like the Strat v60 dashboard and Phantom's 'trend joins'; the rules are ours.
strategies.verdict: Needs about 80% winners just to break even. Needs 1-minute candles.

strategies.name: VWAP band fade
strategies.rules: A close outside VWAP plus or minus 2 standard deviations, then a close back inside; target VWAP; up to 2 a day.
strategies.source: Phantom's 'fades'; the rules are ours.
strategies.verdict: Best-looking first read (30 trades), which is still an anecdote.

strategies.name: Failed breakout
strategies.rules: A candle pokes through yesterday's high or low and closes back inside; target 2R; each level once a day.
strategies.source: Phantom's 'failed breakouts'; the rules are ours.
strategies.verdict: Lost on the first read (9 trades).

strategies.name: Noise-area momentum
strategies.rules: Go with price when it leaves its usual range for that time of day (last 14 days); trailing stop; flat at the close; 1% emergency stop.
strategies.source: Zarattini, Aziz & Barbon (Swiss Finance Institute). Independent futures test 2020 to Oct 2026: about 6.8 points a trade on Nasdaq after costs, every year positive. Plan bot 1: build first.
strategies.verdict: The strongest outside evidence of anything here, and the only family the factory let through on its first night (6 survivors, PBO 29%). Still weeks of data, a falling market, and samples just over 30 trades. Drawdowns can last over a year.

evidence.note: First 22 trades +$1,425, last 22 trades +$31. Too short to judge.

evidence.data: MNQ 15m, 1 Sep to 17 Nov 2026: tuned on 33 sessions, judged on 23 unseen sessions from 16 Oct
evidence.note: 6 of 32 variations survived every factory check (PBO 29%), including the paper's own settings (14 days, x1, half-hourly): +$839 on 32 unseen trades. The best unseen was +$1,814 (21 days, x0.8). The unseen weeks include the October to November sell-off, which suits momentum. Promotion needs 5 nights in a row.

strategies.next: Owner's NinjaTrader Strategy Analyzer run from 2019 (quint-control/proof/README.md).

strategies.name: RSI(2) all-weather (saved on TraderDev as '[retest] QQQ COMBO RSI2 all-weather 1h')
strategies.market: MNQ (tested on QQQ stand-in and real MNQ)
strategies.rules: Long when close is above the 200 SMA and RSI(2) is under 5, exit on a close above the 10 SMA. Short when close is below the 200 SMA and RSI(2) is over 93, exit on a close below the 10 SMA. No stop loss. Holds overnight.
strategies.source: TraderDev strategy 01M5062BVT82A1S9JC7GFJ8F9S, from an earlier Claude chat. Classic Connors RSI(2) idea.
strategies.verdict: Rejected as it stands: on real MNQ it lost money, its worst drawdown was 2.5 times Lucid's max loss, and it has no stop loss. The long side alone made a little, which is a new idea to test on untouched data, not a result.

strategies.rules: See each strategy's Pine source on TraderDev.
strategies.source: TraderDev strategies 01M5062HGH4YX8NPYF8NTX4BZK, 01M5062KTTV9AQ1A9ZHMG9DG9H, 01M5062F6Y0S7GRBWPM9C5TDZQ, 01M5062DJ3D6CQM4HP66VHDBJJ, 01M50629VR3DXCVVF48DPB4WMD.
strategies.verdict: All look positive once TraderDev's crypto fees are swapped for MNQ costs (rough: squeeze +$9,677, mean-reversion +$7,078, EMA ATR +$5,728, pivot +$2,707, trend pullback +$12,408), but only on the QQQ stand-in, whose overnight hours are thin. strategies.name: Lucid MNQ sweep + volume (TraderDev)
strategies.rules: A sweep of a 10-bar swing high or low on 1.5x average volume that closes back inside; stop beyond the wick; target 2R; Lucid-style daily limits.
strategies.source: TraderDev strategies 01M504KRFHDZ4MPQGSTMVC0SWP (v2) and 01M504HX0K0GZM5BGJCRRTE03H (v1).
strategies.verdict: Rejected for now: 16 trades in six months and about break-even before costs. Liquidity-grab signals also failed the 947-day MNQ study. Version 1 can't run on TraderDev (it uses strategy.closedtrades.profit).

evidence.note: Already sized like 1 MNQ, so close to real dollars.

strategies.next: None. The 5-pillar playbook covers this idea better.

strategies.name: RSI(2) pullback, daily
strategies.rules: Buy a sharp short dip inside an uptrend, sell on the bounce.
strategies.source: Plan bot 8. Positive over 10 years on the S&P 500 (PF 1.43) but only 1.7% a year (Backtrex).
strategies.verdict: Holds overnight, so only where the account allows it (research/prop-firms/OVERNIGHT-FUTURES.md).
strategies.next: Daily data back to 2019 is already in lab/data, so this one can be tested without TradingView calls.

strategies.name: Long-term trend following
strategies.rules: Hold the direction of the 3 to 12 month trend.
strategies.source: The best evidence of all: trend profits in 58 futures (AQR).
strategies.verdict: Deep drawdowns that trailing-drawdown prop accounts punish. A personal-account idea for later.

queue.what: Grow the MNQ candle store every night with one TradingView call: the newest 5-minute candles, merged into lab/data; the 15-minute candles are built from them. This feeds the paper forward test and the strategy factory.

Run the strategy factory every night (lab/FACTORY.md): every variation of every family, judged on unseen sessions, PBO, neighbours, double costs and the Lucid gate. Variations that survive 5 nights in a row get a registry entry and a frozen paper forward test.
Get 1-minute MNQ into lab/data, so the WYLD family can confirm on the 1-minute chart as WYLD does. Sources: a NinjaTrader export from the owner's Windows computer, or a data vendor file.
queue.cost: Owner's time or a data purchase

queue.what: Pre-registered 19 Nov 2026, before any result: long only, enter on a close above the 200 SMA with RSI(2) under 5, exit on a close above the 10 SMA, stop 1.5 x ATR(14) below the entry, out after 24 candles at most; 1 MNQ, $0.75 a side, 1 tick slippage, margin 0. Test only on 1 Apr to 19 Nov 2026 MNQ 1h, which no RSI(2) test has traded. Pass: profit after costs, worst drawdown under $2,000, at least 40 trades. Otherwise reject.
Run 'Prop B: RSI(2) combo, Globex day' on real MNQ 1h chart history with margin 0, exactly as saved.

Chart Wizard's older coding of your strategy with a fixed 2R target instead of 'the other side of the range' (REPORT.md next test 2), to see if the room filter is what blocks it. Lower priority than wyld-exact-rules.

The owner runs the 12 bots in NinjaTrader's Strategy Analyzer on 1-minute MNQ from June 2019 (steps in quint-control/botlab/README.md) and sends the result blocks. This is the biggest evidence upgrade available: years of data instead of weeks.
queue.cost: About 30 minutes on the Windows computer

queue.what: Decide how to get years of intraday MNQ in the cloud: TradingView Premium adds Deep Backtesting, or a data vendor file of 1-minute MNQ. Until then, years-long tests happen in NinjaTrader.

Write WYLD Will's Four Pillars as exact rules a computer can test, following his videos: what counts as the easiest equal highs and lows on the 15m, how a level shows it holds, the stop buffer in ticks, the break-even trigger, and the cap on entries per PDR. You answer the gaps in Quint HQ or in chat. Then the Trading Mastery and Chart Wizard versions get lined up with these rules. Nothing is backtested until the rules are fixed.

lessons.lesson: Testing thousands of variations finds lucky winners easily: on the first night breakout and opening range scored PBO 60 to 67%, meaning their best variations were mostly luck. Only judge on unseen sessions, PBO, neighbours and the Lucid gate.

The owner's strategy is WYLD Will's Four Pillars, the master version. Trading Mastery's six steps and Chart Wizard's 5 pillars are older codings of it, not separate strategies. Keep one entry and one checklist.

The QQQ crypto stand-in on TraderDev flatters strategies. RSI(2) all-weather looked like about +$10,000 on 1 MNQ there and lost $2,345 on real MNQ (different months, so not a perfect comparison). Use the stand-in for quick ideas only; judge on real MNQ.
TraderDev forces 0.05% commission a side and 100%-of-equity sizing whatever the script says, 20 to 30 times MNQ's real costs, so its dollar figures are not MNQ dollars. Convert, or re-test elsewhere.
Most TraderDev edges came from the overnight hours, when the stand-in market is thin. The regular-hours versions mostly lost. An edge that only exists in thin hours is a warning sign.

The owner's TradingView plan has no Deep Backtesting: tests use chart history only (about 23 months of 1-hour MNQ). Set margin to 0 in test scripts, or a 1-MNQ test on $50,000 stops trading at a margin call.
Most of the repo's breakout profit came from shorts in the October to November 2026 sell-off. Always check long and short separately and what the market did.
Expect most ideas to fail: 14 common signal families on 947 days of MNQ didn't beat costs (arXiv 2605.04004), and AI price prediction on 5-minute candles was right 50 to 51% of the time.
